differences.title: 1. STORAGE & PERSISTENCE
differences.leftDesc: Kafka stores all events durably on disk in partitioned append-only logs with configurable retention, ensuring replayability across consumers even after crashes or restarts.
differences.rightDesc: Pub/Sub retains messages briefly (configurable retention up to 7 days) but relies on Google's distributed storage; messages older than retention are permanently deleted, limiting replayability.

differences.title: 2. SCALING MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Kafka scales by partitioning topics, distributing partitions across brokers; scalability tied to partition count and broker capacity, requiring manual tuning for optimal throughput.
differences.rightDesc: Pub/Sub scales automatically with publishing/consuming throughput; no partition management needed; Google handles resource allocation transparently based on load.

differences.title: 3. PROTOCOL & CLIENT
differences.leftDesc: Kafka uses a custom binary protocol over TCP optimized for high-throughput binary data exchange, reducing protocol overhead and improving serialization efficiency.
differences.rightDesc: Pub/Sub employs RESTful HTTP/gRPC APIs for all operations, simplifying client integration but introducing higher latency and protocol overhead compared to binary protocols.

differences.title: 4. CONSUMER MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Kafka consumers pull messages at their own pace using offset tracking, enabling precise control over processing order and flow, ideal for batch processing pipelines.
differences.rightDesc: Pub/Sub pushes messages to subscribers in real-time via HTTP callbacks, reducing consumer-side complexity but increasing risk of message loss if endpoints fail after acknowledgment.

differences.title: 5. ORDERING GUARANTEES
differences.leftDesc: Kafka guarantees strict ordering of messages within a partition using a single partition leader for writes; ordering extends only to messages within the same partition/topic.
differences.rightDesc: Pub/Sub does not provide global ordering guarantees; messages across topics/subscriptions may arrive out of order unless ordered delivery is explicitly configured per subscription.

differences.title: 6. SECURITY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Kafka secures clusters via SASL (e.g., PLAIN, SCRAM) for authentication, SSL for encryption, and ACLs for authorization, offering granular access control at topic/partition level.
differences.rightDesc: Pub/Sub integrates with Google Cloud IAM for authentication/authorization, providing policy-based access control but lacks fine-grained topic-level permissions found in Kafka.

differences.title: 7. OPERATIONAL MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Kafka requires operators to manage brokers, zookeeper, monitoring, scaling, and upgrades; deployments span on-prem, cloud VMs, or managed services like Confluent Cloud/AWS MSK.
differences.rightDesc: Pub/Sub is fully managed by Google Cloud; no infrastructure provisioning, patching, or scaling needed; developers only manage topics/subscriptions and client code.
